messages:
mike_sre: noticed a jump in p99 TTFT for token-level SLI in eu-west around 05:10 UTC, +220ms vs baseline. grafana panel shows step at 05:10.
jana_metrics: saw that too. looks correlated with a drop in tokens/sec sampling at the same time. possible sampling bias after last recording-rule change.
mike_sre: any idea which rule? I only see a config push at 04:58 from platform that touched token_exporter rules.
oliver_platform: that was me — I changed the recording rule that aggregates token_latency_seconds_summary to use sum by (le,job,region) instead of sum without region to reduce cardinality. my change rolled at 04:56.
jana_metrics: when you scoped by region we accidentally lost the per-customer pop we relied on for stable histograms; Prometheus then downsampled differently and our histogram_quantile on the panel started returning skewed p99 values.
mike_sre: aha. so it's a cardinality->aggregation interplay causing the tail to look worse, not actual infra regression?
jana_metrics: likely. check raw exemplars: the kv-cache host-level latencies are fine in logs. here's the promql we had on dashboard:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))
```

and oliver's new rule produces a higher-level sum before rate which changes distribution.

oliver_platform: i can revert but i'd rather update the recording rule to preserve the customer/zone label we need for stable buckets. revert is quick if you want to stabilize now.
sre-oncall: for immediate mitigation we should mute the p99 alert or raise threshold while we fix query. Ops: i'll silence the alert for eu-west for 30m.
mike_sre: pls do; also create a short-lived dashboard panel using raw series (no recording rule) to validate real signal vs aggregated one.
jana_metrics: created a temp panel and compared. raw shows p99 +20ms, panel shows +220ms. 10x difference -> definitely query artifact.
deploy-bot: Deployment oliver_platform/recording-rule-update v2 rolled successfully at 04:56:43 UTC (sha: a1b2c3). :white_check_mark:
oliver_platform: i'm reverting to previous rule now and will craft new rule that keeps region and customer_id for the histograms. deploying revert.
deploy-bot: Revert oliver_platform/recording-rule-revert v1 started at 05:22:10 UTC.

jana_metrics: proposed rule snippet to keep labels but avoid cardinality explosion:

```
- record: token_latency:bucket:sum
  expr: sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, zone)
```

we'll keep region+zone, drop per-request customer_id from the recording rule and instead use labels in dashboards by joining with a separate series if needed.
mike_sre: sounds good. add a Grafana note and annotate the 05:10 spike as "aggregation-rule change" so alerts/owners know it's not infra.
sre-oncall: alert muted for eu-west token-p99-ttft for 30m. i'll follow up with postmortem note in #incidents if revert doesn't stabilize.
oliver_platform: revert finished at 05:28:44 UTC. please reload dashboards. i'll open a PR with the conservative recording rule and tests for histogram stability.
jana_metrics: reloaded — temp panel matches raw now, p99 back to ~baseline (+25ms). leaving the temp panel for 24h and will run a sampling-sensitivity test.
mike_sre: great. action items:
- oliver: PR for safer recording rule, include tests (owner: oliver_platform)
- jana: sampling-sensitivity test + dashboard temp panel (owner: jana_metrics)
- sre-oncall: short postmortem note + alert tuning follow-up (owner: sre-oncall)
- mike: annotate grafana spike and update runbook with this class of failure

sre-oncall: noted. will close this thread when PR merged and metrics stable for 1h.
